P1.evidence: No setter notes were read back, and the prospect opened by complaining about the handoff: 'your administrator that I spoke to a few days ago, wasn't very forthcoming in terms of options... She didn't really give very much details nor did she ask for any pertinent points.' The rep neither acknowledged that nor bridged from it. The frame itself was the richest in the batch — 'understanding exactly what's going on with your fitness right now. What are you looking to improve? What are your goals? What's working? What's not? What have you tried?' — three of the four parts, missing only what you need. Agreement asked and given ('That sound good?' → 'Yep'). Open question ran, though slightly out of order, before the frame.

P2.evidence: Work was interrogated more thoroughly here than on any other call in the batch — the rep pushed through a confusing answer with 'I'm confused. So you say you're self-employed, and you do something about skincare and then acting. What did you mean by what you just said?' and kept going until he had the two income streams, the agency mechanics, the frequency of bookings and the fact that the clinic had closed. Injuries also credit: the knee was volunteered but the rep ran real follow-ups, establishing the pending surgery, the eighteen-month duration, the functional restriction and load tolerance ('Is that limiting the types of exercises and movements you can do?', 'Can you weight on it, like your knee?'). Training week fully mapped. Against that, no age, height or weight at all; no general health conditions or medication question beyond the knee; and no diet question whatsoever despite fat loss being the entire stated goal. No sleep, no energy.

P3.evidence: Thin on the physical layer and the deepest work of the batch on the psychological one. The rep asked the aesthetic goal precisely ('Are we talking like a six pack?') and then never touched mobility, strength or energy. But the bridge was pursued through two vague answers rather than abandoned: 'Where is the motivation coming from to work, to start transforming that right now?' → deflection, then 'is there something that, let's say, maybe the shape you're in is affecting in some other part of your life?' → the acting work, then 'is there anything else?' → the morale. He then reached identity explicitly and at length — 'it's like a different identity, you know? They always say that's like the highest driver of human behavior' — and closed with a clean reflect-back and tie-down: 'To me, it sounds like the issue at hand is your motivation is coming from external sources... It's more of an external motivation versus an internal' followed by 'Anything you would disagree with or add?' → 'there's an element of truth to that.' Who else it impacts was never asked, which mattered given the isolation he had just described.

P4.evidence: Fully run. 'When was the last time that you consistently... did you have a gym routine before or did you have any other thing where you were more motivated and you were in better shape? And then also, what were you doing differently, if anything?' produced the answer — that a separate workplace forced him out of the house and created both the exercise and the reason to look presentable. The rep then pressed on the mechanism rather than accepting it: 'what was the additional motivator? Or was it having to be presentable in public? Or were you more motivated by being around other people? I'm trying to understand what was different back then versus now.' The prospect named the gap himself and confirmed it twice: 'motivation is probably one of the stronger elements which is holding me back' and 'it's kind of harder to self-motivate and it's always something that is a result of a stimuli.' P4f ran in substance through the whole external-versus-internal exchange.

P5.evidence: The only P5 in this batch that is not a straight miss, and it still only part-credits. The rep did project the pattern forward and name the cost of it repeating: 'I'm guessing that you don't want to just lose weight and get in better shape, and then gain it back again... it's still the same pattern, which is like, okay, once that no longer becomes a motivator, either you find another external motivator that's pushing you enough to go back to the gym, or what happens? Most likely just go back to unmotivated, kind of fall out of it.' That is a cost-of-inaction projection in substance. What did not run is any of it as a question the prospect had to answer — no two-year frame, no 'is that something you're willing to settle for', no 'why not', no line in the sand. It was delivered as the rep's analysis rather than extracted as the prospect's own conclusion.

P6.evidence: The belief question was asked — 'do you feel like that's what you're looking for, or how do you feel?' — and produced an honest no: 'Whether I'm actually there in my mindset and other aspects, I'm not sure. I suppose that's the only area that's kind of holding me back.' Correctly surfaced, then not worked. The all-in question never ran. P6c part-credits because the rep genuinely did not move forward without a yes, which is the rule being followed rather than broken; but the script's remedy on hesitation is to return to Phase 5, and instead he moved to disqualification.

P11.evidence: No close was attempted and none should have been. The rep chose not to price the offer once the prospect disclosed financial hardship, so the phase was never reachable. This is a genuine not-applicable rather than a failure, and it should not count against the rep in the denominator.

objection_plays.detail: The trigger fired — 'I am struggling, in all honesty' — and none of the play ran: no isolate, no should-I-versus-how frame, no permission-to-be-honest question, and no financial picture. Recorded as a miss for consistency of scoring, but a coach should not act on it. Running an open-wallet financial inventory on someone who has just said he cannot pay his bills is the wrong move, and the rep's actual response was better than the script: he named the price band honestly, pointed the prospect at free content and said 'I don't want to, like, take your last dollars to do this.' The finding here belongs to the playbook, not the rep.

Doubt was directed at himself rather than the programme: 'Whether I'm actually there in my mindset and other aspects, I'm not sure.' The rep had already done most of the conceptual work for this ten minutes earlier through the internal-versus-external motivation and quality-of-fuel framing, and the prospect engaged with it seriously. But none of the scripted moves ran — no certainty question, no pleasure-versus-pain frame, no bridge, no 'how will you know if you never actually try' — and crucially he did not return to any of it once the prospect named the doubt as his blocker.

Clinical fit, unscripted. The prospect is on a waiting list for a ligament or tendon replacement in his right knee. There is no scripted path for establishing whether kettlebell training is appropriate before surgery, no clearance question anywhere in the process, and the rep both described the programme and recommended free unsupervised YouTube and Instagram workouts without addressing it, including the line 'there's really no excuse not to do it, unless you want to make one.'

Financial hardship with no capacity anywhere, which the playbook does not contemplate — Objection C assumes funds exist somewhere in the picture. The rep improvised a graceful disqualification that protected the prospect and the brand, gave him a genuinely useful free alternative, and left the relationship intact ('As long as you get some value out of this call, that's the main thing' → 'Brilliant. Yeah. Appreciate that. Thank you.'). This is a gap in the script that should be closed with a standard disqualification path, and this call is the template for it.

notes: Strongest Phase 4 and the only Phase 5 in the batch that scores above zero, plus the best judgement call of the batch in declining to sell to someone in hardship. Two corrections that cost nothing: ask the diet question when the entire goal is a leaner midsection, and price the secondary product before disqualifying — Primal University was raised and never quoted, so an affordable route was closed off without being tested. And a pending knee ligament replacement needs a clearance question before any training, paid or free, is recommended.
